A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, core sampler, and several experiments. All text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A–C were included in the inspection.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet results in Table 1, Jacobian and gradient-direction experiments in Figures 2–3, and layer-inference examples in Figure 5.

after.justification: V2 reports original inverse-problem, style-guided, and mask-guided results in Tables 1–4, plus convergence experiments, ablations, and qualitative studies in its appendices.

M1.justification: The core finite-difference sampler remains, but v1's separate layer-inference algorithm, involving soft-mask sampling and per-layer Gaussian likelihoods, is removed. V2 introduces task-specific guidance using CLIP Gram-matrix losses, segmentation KL divergence, and a non-differentiable quantization rule. These substantially change the set of proposed procedures.

E1.justification: ImageNet free-form inpainting and 8× super-resolution remain. V2 adds 25% box inpainting, style-guided generation using WikiArt and PartiPrompts, mask-guided generation using FFHQ, and a quantized-image toy task. V1's layer-decomposition experiments on web images disappear.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds FreeDoM and MPGD while removing the fine-tuned inpainting comparator there; the matched Figure 4 drops DPS. New style/mask comparisons evaluate DDIM, FreeDoM, and/or MPGD, and Appendix C.5 includes naive pixel replacement for box inpainting. Table 1 retains P2L, LDPS, and PSLD.

E3.justification: The retained ImageNet benchmark changes from Stable Diffusion 1.5 to 1.4 and from 1,000 randomly selected ctest10k images to the first 1,000. New protocols evaluate 1,000 style–prompt pairs with style and CLIP scores, and 100 FFHQ references with mIoU and CLIP-FID. These are substantial setting and evaluation-design changes.

E4.justification: V1's Jacobian-asymmetry and grid-update analyses are retained and expanded. V2 adds eigenvalue/convergence experiments and single-pixel influence visualizations in Appendix A, optimization-step and learning-rate ablations in Table 5, a five-versus-twenty-update convergence study in Appendix C.4, and CLIP/OpenCLIP guidance comparisons.

E5.justification: V2 newly states that the grid-update experiment is repeated across multiple seeds, illustrated in Figure 20. V1 does not disclose such repetition. This is limited qualitative replication; neither version supplies benchmark confidence intervals or significance tests, and an increase in benchmark runs is not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the proposed method's free-form FID of 30.45 with 19.39 and super-resolution PSNR of 22.29 with 24.26 under changed settings. Its reported times change from approximately two minutes to 15 seconds/one minute; LDPS/PSLD times change from eight/twelve to six/eight minutes. Tables 2–5 add substantial results, while layer-inference results disappear. These are not controlled cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 replaces v1's local inverse-function derivation with generalized Gauss–Newton equations, inverse/pseudoinverse assumptions, and an explicit approximation using J e. Appendix A.1 adds an inexact-Newton residual condition and spectral analysis based on an almost-symmetric Jacobian. This is substantial new mathematical reasoning, although the convergence argument remains approximate.

C1.justification: Fast constrained sampling without denoiser backpropagation remains central. However, v1's explicitly claimed layer-inference contribution is dropped, and v2 foregrounds linear and nonlinear conditioning applications. The abstract's comparison scope also shifts from state-of-the-art tuned models to training-free inference methods, substantially revising the contribution framing.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of MPGD's difficulty propagating spatially localized constraints, learning-rate overshoot, the Jacobian's proposed regularizing effect, and P2L's texture advantage. It also discusses style-versus-text and mask-fidelity-versus-realism tradeoffs, and acknowledges limitations relative to face-specific models. These extend v1's much narrower interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 adds an implementation link, explicit mask-dilation details, DDIM step counts, optimization and guidance settings, critic-model variants, and expanded sampling pseudocode. These substantially improve documentation without proving that every newly stated setting changed. V1's warm-restart and super-resolution perturbation descriptions disappear, without explicitly establishing that those operations stopped being used.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against FreeDoM and MPGD, distinguishing costly denoiser backpropagation from faster updates that inadequately propagate constraints. It adds inexact-Newton and Arnoldi references and extensive guidance/style-generation context. Earlier fine-tuning references, including Xie et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2024), are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. The Jacobian discussions are consolidated, the experimental narrative is reorganized around linear, style, and mask constraints, and Appendices A–C organize supporting material. V1's unfinished explanatory passages are also replaced.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text to two columns, merges Figure 2's three scatterplots into a color-coded plot, rearranges Figure 3, and revises Figure 4's comparison grid. The layer-decomposition display disappears, while new comparison tables, diagnostic plots, and inference sequences substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited validation of general constraints and incomplete implementation documentation through nonlinear comparisons, parameter ablations, detailed settings, and an implementation link. The expanded explanations make the method and its tradeoffs easier to assess. Although layer inference is dropped and the convergence analysis remains approximate, the empirical and documentation gains substantially improve overall quality. Changed ImageNet settings prevent attributing this improvement simply to revised Table 1 scores.
